title: Lightweight TPS microbenchmark harness with p95 regression detection
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a lightweight tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark harness focused on stable, repeatable measurements across core served models and an automated p95 regression detector. This ticket covers the harness, CI integration, baseline capture job, and alerting for regressions.

Background: Existing microbench artifacts (ENG-5931, ENG-7824) provide throughput and sustained load data but are heavy and not easily run in quick guard-rails. We need a fast runner developers and CI can invoke that returns TPS, p95 latency, sample distributions, and a regression signal compared against a golden baseline. The harness must be resilient to noise (warmup, KV-cache priming, stable RNG seeds) and be simple to extend for new model sizes.

Scope and constraints:
- Core models only (small/medium/large variants we serve).
- Must run in <= 10 minutes on a single test GPU (or cost-simulated CPU path for local dev).
- Deterministic synthetic prompt sets stored in repo.
- Output JSON summary with TPS, p50/p95/p99, token counts, and run metadata.
- Regression detector to compare against stored baseline with configurable thresholds and a basic alert (Slack/GH issue) when p95 drops by >10% or TPS drops by >12%.
- CI job that runs nightly and posts results to benchmark dashboard and creates a blocking PR comment if regression detected.
acceptance_criteria: Harness executable (python or go) committed under tools/benchmarks/tps_harness with README and example config
Produces deterministic JSON output containing fields: model, run_id, tokens_requested, tokens_generated, tps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, env, seed
Baseline capture job runs nightly and stores per-model baselines in benchmarks/baselines/runtime-1.20.json
Automated regression detection that opens a GitHub issue and posts to #benchmarks Slack when thresholds exceeded
CI job (gha) that can be manually triggered in PRs and runs within 10 minutes on the dedicated test GPU image
Documentation for adding a new model variant and tuning the thresholds is included in tools/benchmarks/README.md
updates: 2025-02-11: Spike completed comparing Python vs Go runner latency overhead. Python with async aiohttp chosen for faster iteration.
2025-02-12: Synthetic prompt set curated (50 prompts across lengths 8/32/128 tokens); KV-cache priming strategy defined (3 warmup requests per prompt).
2025-02-14: Baseline schema approved by runtime team; decided to store percentiles and rolling std to handle noise.
2025-02-16: Initial CI job prototype posts JSON to S3 and triggers Lambda for regression check; working on converting to GH Actions for visibility.
2025-02-18: Added p95 guard with default threshold 10% and TPS guard 12%; documenting alert flow and ownership (oncall-runtime).
